 Pacific Notes: Murray, Black, Hachimura, Ighodaro
 By Eli Cohen |
 at November 8, 2026 5:02 pm 
 Keegan Murray is suiting up for the Kings in their game on Sunday against the Heat, reports ESPN’s James Ham ( via Twitter ).
 The 26-year-old forward has played just two games for the Kings this season while dealing with left ankle capsulitis , starting the first two games of the season before missing the next seven.
 Murray has struggled with injuries recently, playing just 23 games in the 2025/26 season after playing at least 75 games each of his first three seasons in the league.
 He has also struggled to find consistent offense. After shooting 41.1% on 6.3 attempts per game as a rookie, his outside shooting numbers have decreased in each consecutive year. He will rejoin a Kings team that could benefit from him rediscovering his outside shot.
 In Murray’s absence, Precious Achiuwa has stepped into the starting power forward spot, averaging 10.8 points, 5.9 rebounds, and 1.2 blocks per game.
 We have more from around the Pacific Division:
 After trading Nique Clifford to the Thunder for two second-round picks, the Kings need to add another player on a guaranteed deal to get to 14 standard roster spots. They have 14 days to do so, and they’re going to use that time to carefully evaluate their next addition, according to Ham ( via Twitter ). One candidate to secure a standard deal, Ham notes, is two-way forward Leaky Black . The 27-year-old small forward has played five games with the Kings this season, including one start, and has averaged 5.8 points and 1.6 steals in 19.0 minutes per game while hitting 44.4% of his threes.
 Rui Hachimura is averaging career highs in points (14.7), rebounds (6.5), steals (1.0), free-throw attempts (3.2), and three-point attempts (6.3) this season for the Clippers  as he has stepped into a role as a featured player. He has also developed a level of trust with head coach Ty Lue , which can be traced back to a trip Lue took to Japan this summer to establish chemistry with his new forward, writes Ohm Youngmisuk for NBA.com. There, Hachimura had Lue try some of his favorite dishes while the two tried to get to know each other. “ Without him saying anything [to me], he was trying to be more open with me,” Hachimura said. “ I think that’s one thing about my culture that is different. We’re not really open with people. We‘re closed off basically. We don’t really share information. We don’t really talk about emotion, talk about things that you want to do [personally]. That’s the thing that he is trying — to be more open with me. And I’m trying to [do the same.] ” Hachimura’s role is likely to change with the impending return of Brandon Ingram , but the connection he established with Lue will hopefully help him navigate the new responsibilities.
 The Suns recently made a move to try to shake things up following a 1-5 start to the season. They moved second-year big man Khaman Maluach back to the bench and elevated Oso Ighodaro into the starting slot, and the team responded with a win over the Magic that snapped a four-game losing streak. “ Just making an adjustment, just to change things up, just to try to figure out how we get 48 minutes of great center play ,” head coach Jordan Ott continued. “ And I thought both of them handled it well. [Maluach] obviously had one of his better games. Yeah, we’ll keep trying to find it .”
